section: Mughal architecture - Fatehpur Sikri, Humayun's tomb, Taj Mahal, Red Fort; garden and tomb traditions
subsections: Tomb traditions → builder (Sher Shah, Itimad-ud-Daula, Bibi ka Maqbara) - Lodi to Mughal evolution
Fatehpur Sikri buildings → purpose and style influence

accepted.s: Who completed the tomb of Sher Shah Suri at Sasaram after Sher Shah's death?
accepted.x: Sher Shah Suri's tomb at Sasaram was completed under his son Islam Shah.
accepted.tq: Use the builder-successor distinction to avoid swapping the patron with the person who completed the work.
accepted.sec: Tomb traditions → builder (Sher Shah, Itimad-ud-Daula, Bibi ka Maqbara) - Lodi to Mughal evolution

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Itimad-ud-Daula — Nur Jahan for Mirza Ghiyas Beg
Bibi ka Maqbara — Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal
Sher Shah's tomb — Islam Shah for Babur
Itimad-ud-Daula — Aurangzeb for Dilras Banu Begum
accepted.x: Nur Jahan built the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula for her father, Mirza Ghiyas Beg. Bibi ka Maqbara was built by Prince Azam Shah for his mother, Dilras Banu Begum.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure patron-beneficiary pair and eliminate swapped builders and occupants.
accepted.sec: Tomb traditions → builder (Sher Shah, Itimad-ud-Daula, Bibi ka Maqbara) - Lodi to Mughal evolution

accepted.s: Bibi ka Maqbara, popularly called the “Taj of the Deccan”, was built by:
accepted.x: Prince Azam Shah, son of Aurangzeb, built Bibi ka Maqbara for his mother, Dilras Banu Begum, at Aurangabad.
accepted.tq: Test the builder directly against nearby Mughal and Sur patrons.
accepted.sec: Tomb traditions → builder (Sher Shah, Itimad-ud-Daula, Bibi ka Maqbara) - Lodi to Mughal evolution

accepted.s: Which development is associated with the Sayyid-Lodi tomb tradition?
o: Introduction of Hindu-style gates and facades
Construction of the first double dome
Exclusive use of white marble and pietra dura
accepted.x: Sayyid-Lodi tombs incorporated Hindu elements such as Hindu-style gates and facades, plaster ornament and drip-stones.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive architectural contribution rather than the later Mughal features.
accepted.sec: Tomb traditions → builder (Sher Shah, Itimad-ud-Daula, Bibi ka Maqbara) - Lodi to Mughal evolution

accepted.s: Which monument marked the transition from the Lodi tradition to the Mughal architectural tradition under the Sur rulers?
accepted.x: Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram marks the Sur transition in the evolution of Indo-Islamic tomb architecture.
accepted.tq: Use the historical transition clue to connect the monument with the correct dynasty.
accepted.sec: Tomb traditions → builder (Sher Shah, Itimad-ud-Daula, Bibi ka Maqbara) - Lodi to Mughal evolution

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about early Mughal tomb architecture:
1. Humayun's tomb was the first garden tomb.
2. Humayun's tomb introduced the double dome.
3. Itimad-ud-Daula's tomb was the first Mughal tomb in white marble.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Humayun's tomb introduced the garden-tomb and double-dome traditions, while Itimad-ud-Daula's tomb was the first Mughal tomb in white marble.
accepted.tq: Check each architectural milestone separately before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Tomb traditions → builder (Sher Shah, Itimad-ud-Daula, Bibi ka Maqbara) - Lodi to Mughal evolution

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with Itimad-ud-Daula's tomb?
o: It was built by Aurangzeb at Khuldabad as a simple grave.
It was built by Prince Azam Shah for his mother at Aurangabad.
It was built by Sher Shah at Sasaram and set in a tank.
It was built by Nur Jahan for her father and is known as the “Baby Taj”.
accepted.x: Itimad-ud-Daula's tomb at Agra was built by Nur Jahan for her father, Mirza Ghiyas Beg, and is popularly called the “Baby Taj”.
accepted.tq: Separate similar tomb traditions by matching the builder, beneficiary, place and popular title.
accepted.sec: Tomb traditions → builder (Sher Shah, Itimad-ud-Daula, Bibi ka Maqbara) - Lodi to Mughal evolution

accepted.s: Babur's final tomb is located at:
accepted.x: Babur's tomb is at Bagh-e-Babur in Kabul, although he was first buried at Agra.
accepted.tq: Watch the distinction between the first burial place and the final tomb location.
accepted.sec: Emperor → tomb location (Babur to Aurangzeb)

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Shah Jahan is buried in the Taj Mahal at Agra beside Mumtaz Mahal. Sikandra near Agra is associated with Akbar's tomb.
accepted.tq: Find the wrongly shifted emperor-location pair among otherwise familiar tomb sites.
accepted.sec: Emperor → tomb location (Babur to Aurangzeb)

accepted.s: Aurangzeb's tomb is distinguished from the grand Mughal mausoleums because it is:
o: A marble tomb at Agra beside Mumtaz Mahal
A simple grave at Khuldabad near Aurangabad
accepted.x: Aurangzeb was buried in a simple grave at Khuldabad near Aurangabad.
accepted.tq: Use the contrast between Aurangzeb's simple grave and the monumental Mughal tombs.
accepted.sec: Emperor → tomb location (Babur to Aurangzeb)

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the tombs of Mughal emperors is correct?
o: Jahangir's tomb is at Shahdara in Lahore.
Humayun's tomb is at Sikandra near Agra.
Babur's final tomb is at Shahdara in Lahore.
Aurangzeb's tomb is beside Mumtaz Mahal in Agra.
accepted.x: Jahangir's tomb is located at Shahdara in Lahore. Humayun's tomb is in Delhi, Babur's final tomb is in Kabul and Aurangzeb's grave is at Khuldabad.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among closely related emperor-tomb locations rather than relying on the city alone.
accepted.sec: Emperor → tomb location (Babur to Aurangzeb)

accepted.s: Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar primarily in honour of:
accepted.x: Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri as his new capital in honour of Sheikh Salim Chishti.
accepted.tq: Match the capital city with the saint whose association motivated its construction.
accepted.sec: Fatehpur Sikri buildings → purpose and style influence

accepted.s: The principal material used in the construction of Fatehpur Sikri was:
accepted.x: Fatehpur Sikri was constructed mainly of red sandstone.
accepted.tq: Use the material contrast between Akbar's red-sandstone phase and Shah Jahan's marble phase.
accepted.sec: Fatehpur Sikri buildings → purpose and style influence

accepted.s: Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was constructed to commemorate Akbar's:
o: Victory at the Second Battle of Panipat
Accession to the throne at Kalanaur
accepted.x: Buland Darwaza, meaning the “Gate of Magnificence”, commemorated Akbar's victory in the Gujarat conquest.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the commemorated event from other major events of Akbar's reign.
accepted.sec: Fatehpur Sikri buildings → purpose and style influence

accepted.s: Which building at Fatehpur Sikri served as a house of worship where scholars of different religions held philosophical debates?
accepted.x: The Ibadat Khana was the House of Worship used for philosophical debates among scholars of various religions.
accepted.tq: Match the building with its precise institutional purpose.
accepted.sec: Fatehpur Sikri buildings → purpose and style influence

accepted.s: The Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri was built in:
accepted.x: The Ibadat Khana was built in 1575.
accepted.tq: Separate the dates of capital planning and construction from the specific date of the Ibadat Khana.
accepted.sec: Fatehpur Sikri buildings → purpose and style influence

accepted.s: Jodha Bai's palace at Fatehpur Sikri illustrates the combination of:
o: Hindu trabeate and Islamic arcuate styles
Buddhist stupa and Jain temple styles
Persian dome and Turkish minaret styles only
accepted.x: Jodha Bai's palace combines Hindu trabeate construction, based on beams and lintels, with Islamic arcuate construction, based on arches and domes.
accepted.tq: Distinguish trabeate and arcuate systems by their structural elements.
accepted.sec: Fatehpur Sikri buildings → purpose and style influence

accepted.s: Which feature is characteristic of the Diwan-i-Khas at Fatehpur Sikri?
o: A five-storeyed pavilion with Persian wind towers
A single central carved pillar supporting a throne platform
A gateway commemorating the Gujarat conquest
A white-marble tomb in the Jami Masjid courtyard
accepted.x: The Diwan-i-Khas is known for its single central carved pillar supporting a throne platform.
accepted.tq: Use the unique central-pillar feature to identify the correct building.
accepted.sec: Fatehpur Sikri buildings → purpose and style influence

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Fatehpur Sikri:
1. It was planned as Akbar's capital during 1571–1585.
2. Its buildings show Persian, Indian and Central Asian influences.
3. Akbar introduced the Tudor or four-centred arch in his buildings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Fatehpur Sikri was Akbar's planned capital during 1571–1585 and reflects multiple architectural influences, including the Tudor arch introduced by Akbar.
accepted.tq: Test chronology, stylistic synthesis and a specific architectural innovation together.
accepted.sec: Fatehpur Sikri buildings → purpose and style influence

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pietra dura — inlay of semi-precious stones
Double dome — inner and outer shells
accepted.x: Jali refers to lattice work. Mirror-work chambers are associated with the Sheesh Mahal.
accepted.tq: Separate related decorative terms by their exact meanings and locations.
accepted.sec: Architectural features - double dome, pietra dura, charbagh, synthesis, sandstone vs marble

accepted.s: The charbagh garden tradition in Mughal architecture was introduced by:
accepted.x: Babur introduced the charbagh, or four-quartered garden, tradition; Ram Bagh at Agra is an example.
accepted.tq: Match the architectural innovation with the earliest Mughal ruler associated with it.
accepted.sec: Architectural features - double dome, pietra dura, charbagh, synthesis, sandstone vs marble

accepted.s: Pietra dura refers to:
o: The construction of a dome with two shells
The division of a garden into four quarters
The use of lattice screens for ventilation
accepted.x: Pietra dura is the technique of inlaying semi-precious stones in architectural surfaces.
accepted.tq: Test the exact technical meaning of a commonly confused architectural term.
accepted.sec: Architectural features - double dome, pietra dura, charbagh, synthesis, sandstone vs marble

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the development of pietra dura in Mughal architecture?
o: It began under Jahangir, appeared on a large scale at Itimad-ud-Daula and reached its peak at the Taj Mahal.
It began under Babur and reached its peak at Sher Shah's tomb.
It began under Akbar and was confined to red sandstone buildings.
It began under Aurangzeb and reached its peak at Bibi ka Maqbara.
accepted.x: Pietra dura began during Jahangir's reign, was first used on a large scale at Itimad-ud-Daula and reached its peak at the Taj Mahal.
accepted.tq: Arrange the beginning, large-scale use and culmination of a style in sequence.
accepted.sec: Architectural features - double dome, pietra dura, charbagh, synthesis, sandstone vs marble

accepted.s: The Persian-Indian synthesis in Mughal architecture is best represented by the combination of:
o: Only European columns and Gothic vaults
Arches and domes with trabeate forms, chhatris and Hindu motifs
Only Buddhist stupas and Jain shikharas
accepted.x: The Persian-Indian synthesis combined arches and domes with trabeate forms, chhatris and Hindu motifs, as seen at Fatehpur Sikri and Akbar's tomb.
accepted.tq: Translate the stylistic definition into its constituent architectural elements.
accepted.sec: Architectural features - double dome, pietra dura, charbagh, synthesis, sandstone vs marble

accepted.s: Which comparison between the architectural phases of Akbar and Shah Jahan is correct?
o: Akbar is associated mainly with red sandstone, whereas Shah Jahan is associated mainly with white marble.
Akbar is associated mainly with white marble, whereas Shah Jahan is associated mainly with red sandstone.
Both rulers used only white marble.
Both rulers used only red sandstone.
accepted.x: Akbar's phase is represented by red-sandstone structures such as Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri, while Shah Jahan's phase is dominated by white marble, as in the Taj Mahal.
accepted.tq: Use the material contrast to distinguish the architectural phases of the two rulers.
accepted.sec: Architectural features - double dome, pietra dura, charbagh, synthesis, sandstone vs marble

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the relevant architectural feature?
o: Humayun's tomb — double dome, calligraphy, arabesque and jali work
Taj Mahal — first use of the double dome
accepted.x: Humayun's tomb is associated with the double dome and with calligraphy, arabesque and jali work. The charbagh is a garden form, while the double dome was introduced earlier at Humayun's tomb.
accepted.tq: Combine material, structural and decorative clues to identify the correct monument-feature pair.
accepted.sec: Architectural features - double dome, pietra dura, charbagh, synthesis, sandstone vs marble

accepted.s: Shah Jahan's new capital, Shahjahanabad, included which of the following principal monuments?
o: Sasaram tomb and Bibi ka Maqbara
Agra Fort and Ram Bagh only
accepted.x: Shahjahanabad in Delhi included the Red Fort and the Jama Masjid. Shah Jahan's reign is regarded as the Golden Age of Mughal architecture.
accepted.tq: Identify the components of the capital rather than confusing them with monuments at Fatehpur Sikri or Agra.
accepted.sec: Red Fort and Shahjahanabad - components

accepted.s: The Diwan-i-Am in the Red Fort was meant for:
accepted.x: The Diwan-i-Am was the hall of public audience. The Diwan-i-Khas was the hall of private audience.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the public and private audience halls by their functions.
accepted.sec: Red Fort and Shahjahanabad - components

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Diwan-i-Khas of the Red Fort is correct?
o: It was the residence of the royal women and was called the Palace of Colours.
It housed the Peacock Throne, which was taken by Nadir Shah in 1739.
It was built by Aurangzeb as the Moti Masjid.
It was the public audience hall of Shah Jahan.
accepted.x: The Diwan-i-Khas was the private audience hall and housed the Peacock Throne, which was taken by Nadir Shah in 1739.
accepted.tq: Use the famous object-event association while distinguishing the two audience halls.
accepted.sec: Red Fort and Shahjahanabad - components

accepted.s: The Rang Mahal in the Red Fort was intended primarily for:
o: The storage of the Peacock Throne
accepted.x: Rang Mahal, meaning the “Palace of Colours”, was intended for the royal women.
accepted.tq: Translate the building's title and purpose without confusing it with an audience hall.
accepted.sec: Red Fort and Shahjahanabad - components

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two Mughal structures named Moti Masjid?
o: The Moti Masjid in the Red Fort was built by Aurangzeb, whereas the Moti Masjid in Agra Fort was built by Shah Jahan.
The Red Fort Moti Masjid was built by Shah Jahan, whereas the Agra Fort Moti Masjid was built by Aurangzeb.
Both Moti Masjids were built by Akbar in Agra Fort.
Both Moti Masjids were built by Aurangzeb in Delhi.
accepted.x: Aurangzeb built the Moti Masjid in the Red Fort, while Shah Jahan built the Moti Masjid in Agra Fort.
accepted.tq: Resolve the look-alike monument pair by comparing location and builder.
accepted.sec: Red Fort and Shahjahanabad - components

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Rang Mahal — hall of public audience
accepted.x: Sheesh Mahal is associated with mirror-work chambers. Rang Mahal was for the royal women, Diwan-i-Am was for public audience and Diwan-i-Khas was for private audience.
accepted.tq: Match each Red Fort component with its specific function or decorative treatment.
accepted.sec: Red Fort and Shahjahanabad - components

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about forts associated with the Mughal rulers:
1. Agra Fort was begun by Akbar in 1565.
2. Allahabad Fort was built by Akbar in 1583.
3. Lahore Fort was rebuilt by Akbar.
4. The Red Fort at Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Agra Fort was begun in 1565, Allahabad Fort was built in 1583, Lahore Fort was rebuilt by Akbar and the Red Fort at Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.
accepted.tq: Check the ruler, date and location of each fort before selecting the complete code.
accepted.sec: Red Fort and Shahjahanabad - components

accepted.s: Agra Fort, associated with Akbar, was constructed mainly of:
o: Red sandstone and is situated on the Yamuna
Black stone and is situated on the Narmada
Granite and is situated on the Godavari
White marble and is situated on the Ganga
accepted.x: Akbar's Agra Fort was begun in 1565, constructed of red sandstone and situated on the Yamuna. It contains the Diwan-i-Am and Diwan-i-Khas.
accepted.tq: Combine builder, material and river-location clues to identify the correct fort description.
accepted.sec: Red Fort and Shahjahanabad - components
